node.statement: F2 FROBENIUS INVARIANCE + THE ORBIT-MULTIPLICITY EXPLANATION (2026-07-10, campaign cycle 90): E4 closed by proof, and the measured alignment constant EXPLAINED. THEOREM (5 lines, verified to 2e-15 at F_49, F_25, F_81): (S, eps) are invariant under coordinatewise Frobenius phi(c) = (c_i^p) — substituting z = x^{p^{-1} mod n} gives {Tr(phi(c).xbar(x))}_x = {Tr(c.xbar(z))}_z as multisets. CONSEQUENCE 1 (NO-GO #12): E4 — averaging the sign over Frobenius orbits — is VACUOUS: the sign is CONSTANT on orbits; there is nothing to average. Frequency space now carries a proved invariance group of order ~ n*k (twisted scaling, sat 19, times Frobenius). CONSEQUENCE 2 (the explanation): signs constant on orbits of size ~ n*k means the correct random-sign baseline is PER-ORBIT: predicted alignment ratio = sqrt(n*k) * O(1), NOT O(1). MEASURED COLLAPSE: all 13 banked struct-subtracted ratios (satellite 20) divided by sqrt(n) land in [0.04, 1.56] — eleven in [0.55, 1.56] tightly around 1, and the two below-band rows are exactly the zero-extras rows ((113,16,3) and (769,64,2)); the three prime-power rows divided by sqrt(n*k) give 1.53, 1.00, 0.24. The mysterious 'alignment ~7' of satellites 19-20 IS the orbit multiplicity. THE REFINED SUMMIT MODEL (sharpest falsifiable form): the parity field is RANDOM PER ORBIT with constant ~ 1; refined falsifier — the per-orbit constant (struct-sub ratio / sqrt(n k)) sustained above ~10 at 3+ scales. At official rows the orbit factor sqrt(n k) ~ 2^28 is polynomial in n — harmless to the 2^{o(n)} budget; the summit statement is UNCHANGED in strength but its empirical model is now exact to the measurement floor. Verifier: inline in campaign log #102 (local, small). Twenty-fifth satellite; named lanes remaining: E1 (Ehrhart mod 2), E2 (Dedekind-integer reciprocity). The per-orbit Rademacher model holds through 10M-frequency populations; total verified range now 9.4k to 44M.
